question: In 1932, the Poona Pact was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar, an eminent Indian jurist, economist, politician, and social reformer, played a key role in the anti-caste movement in India.
 
• The Poona Pact was an agreement between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar on behalf of the depressed classes (now known as Scheduled Castes).
 
• The pact was signed on 24th September 1932 in Yerwada Central Jail, Pune.
 
• It aimed at providing reserved seats for the depressed classes in the provincial legislatures within the general electorate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Background of the Poona Pact:**

 
 
• Prior to the Poona Pact, the British government had announced the Communal Award in 1932, which provided separate electorates for minorities and the depressed classes.
 
• Dr. Ambedkar supported the separate electorates as it would provide political representation to the oppressed classes.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi opposed the separate electorates, fearing it would divide Hindu society.
 
• He went on a hunger strike to protest against it, leading to negotiations between Gandhi and Ambedkar.
 
 
 
• **Terms of the Poona Pact:**
 
 
• The Poona Pact provided for a single Hindu electorate, with reserved seats for the depressed classes.
 
• Out of the total 148 seats in the provincial legislatures, 71 seats were reserved for the depressed classes.
 
• Additionally, the pact ensured adequate representation of the depressed classes in the central legislature and other sectors.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Poona Pact:**
 
 
• The pact marked a significant moment in the history of India's struggle for independence, reflecting the internal challenges of caste and social inequality.
 
• It highlighted the efforts to integrate the depressed classes into the mainstream political framework of India.
 
• The agreement paved the way for future affirmative action policies in India aimed at the upliftment of marginalized communities.
